idiom_name: visitor class hierarchy with an is-pattern capability test and a virtual factory method
implementation_notes: C# supplies both halves the pattern needs: virtual methods with bodies, so a visitor class provides default handling that derived visitors inherit, and a runtime type test - the `is` type pattern - that lets a newly added element ask whether the current processor implements its extended interface (Lettieri: `if (processor is IUnionShapeProcessor<T> unionProcessor) return unionProcessor.ForUnionShape(this); throw new NotSupportedException(...)`). An operation is extended by deriving from the existing visitor (`class UnionContainsPoint : ContainsPoint, IUnionShapeProcessor<bool>`), which inherits the base behaviour and adds the new case. Because the extension re-uses inherited code that may create further visitors, the base class must expose a protected virtual factory (`MakeContainsPoint`) so recursion builds the derived visitor instead of the base one; without it the derived case is silently skipped for nested nodes.
pitfalls: The capability test is a runtime check, so a processor that does not implement the extended interface either throws or silently falls back; the write-up insists the default path be explicit rather than a silent no-op.

Recursive visitors must build themselves through the virtual factory: a base visitor that news up its own concrete type drops the derived behaviour on every nested node (the TranslatedShape flaw in the C# case study).

A generic element contract such as T Process<T>(IShapeProcessor<T>) prevents storing element processors in a homogeneous list; if visitors must be mixed, give them a non-generic base with a result object.

variants.name: Versioned visitor interface extended with default interface members
variants.idiom_name: visitor interface grown with default interface members
variants.implementation_notes: C# 8 default interface methods change the economics of the element side: a visit method for a new element kind can be added to the existing visitor interface with a default body that forwards to the previous default case, so implementers that were compiled against the old interface keep working and only those that care override it - Microsoft documents exactly this as the safe way to add members to a released interface. It is the cheapest way to add an element kind when all visitors route unknown cases through a single default member, and it buys the pattern's element-side half without a parallel interface hierarchy. The other half is missing: default interface members are reachable only through the interface, are not inherited by implementing classes, and a default body hides whether an implementer was written against the old or the new version - the APIDesign case study rejects that trade and prefers a new pure versioned interface plus a bridge, so use this variant only for published interfaces you cannot version.
pitfalls: A default interface member can only be called through the interface, so a class that implements IShapeVisitor2 does not expose VisitUnion to ordinary callers, and the implementing class inherits nothing from it.
An interface that overrides a base-interface member must use explicit interface implementation syntax, so a version chain alternates between implicit and explicit members and is easy to get wrong.

The default body hides intent: a visitor that never overrides the new member is indistinguishable from one that deliberately accepts the default, which is why the APIDesign reading rejects this variant for versioned visitor APIs.
